description: Measured 2026-09-14 on interp and run (JIT): a dispatch-pure guard helper 'defp int?(_n :: integer), do: true' used as 'def g(x) when int?(x)' answers :matched for g(:a). The annotated parameter is named with a leading underscore, and its type does not become a plan precondition in reify_guard_dispatch, so the helper admits every value. Repro: scratchpad/8b/t_typed.fz from the 8b research (recreate from this description). Resolved by fz-21x.24, which deletes the reify path: a helper called from a guard is an ordinary call in the guard function's body, and its parameters keep their preconditions like any other parameters. Closes with that commit; the repro becomes a fixture there.
title: Guard helper with a wildcard-named annotated parameter loses its type precondition
